label: 0045 · Smoothed in time, 1997–2025 (one QP over 47 windows): 0044 with a fault mesh and an afterslip state for the 2016 Kumamoto earthquakes, uncorrelated noise, background coupling from −1 to 1, eleven slow slip events as signal, fixed 747-site network, UNR positions (MAP)
description: 0044 on a base experiment with a fault mesh for the 2016 Kumamoto earthquakes (Mw 7.04): the northern Hinagu and Futagawa faults on to Aso, 209 triangles dipping 60–80° northwest from the mapped traces to 30 km. The amur–kuwana block boundary follows the fault, the mainshock gets windows ending 91 and 365 days after it, and the record has a Kumamoto afterslip state with Omori decay (c = 0.05 yr, first-year prior 300 mm/yr). Window cross-validation is 5,549 above the same model without the state and higher in 37 of 47 windows. Residuals within 30 km of the rupture fall from 50 to 6.7 mm/yr in the first 91 days and from 10.1 to 2.4 mm/yr in the rest of the first year. The afterslip is right-lateral and reaches Mw 6.79 in one year and 6.86 in two, but 72% of it lies below 15 km and 29% on the mesh's 30 km bottom row, so the deep part probably stands in for flow in a weak lower crust as well as afterslip. A second state on the BEL sheet beneath the rupture adds at most 105, all in the first window, and isn't kept. Elsewhere the model matches 0044: Tohoku afterslip is Mw 8.26, 8.32 and 8.38 at 1, 2 and 5 years, and the slow slip events are within 0.01 in Mw. Coupling far outside −1 to 1 isn't a real value: in episode windows it is the episodes' strike-slip divided by a small plate rate, and on the Kumamoto mesh after the first year it is afterslip divided by a dip-slip plate rate below 1 mm/yr. MAP solution, no posterior SD.
